summary: James Brooks Jessup specializes in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (circa 2004–2010), where Robert H. Sharf served on his committee.

James Burgess (1832–1916) was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who headed the Archaeological Survey of India starting in 1873, succeeding Alexander Cunningham in 1885. He founded The Indian Antiquary in 1872 and Epigraphia Indica in 1892.

James Burnell Robinson is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (circa 1968–1975) under Richard Hugh Robinson and Geshe Lhundub Sopa, later becoming Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Northern Iowa.

James C. Dobbins works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Yale University (circa 1975–1984) and served as Fairchild Professor of Religion and East Asian Studies at Oberlin College from circa 1983 to 2021.

James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland (1792–1844) was an Indologist. He studied at East India Company College (circa 1807–1809) and Fort William College (circa 1809–1810) under Thomas Roebuck, later serving as professor of law at Presidency University, Kolkata.

James Duerlinger is a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (circa 1964–1968) under Sheldon Pollock and held a post at the University of Iowa from circa 1971 to 2016.
James G. Mullens specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD from McMaster University by circa 1994 and held a post at the University of Saskatchewan in 1989.

James Gibbs (1825–1886) was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1870–1879) and as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai in 1878.

James H. Austin worked in Buddhist studies. He studied under Nanrei Kobori, Joshu Sasaki, and Katsujo Terayama, and held posts at the universities of Oregon (circa 1955–1965), Colorado (circa 1965–1992), Missouri, and Idaho (circa 1992), alongside several sabbatical visits.

James Hadley (1821–1872) was a linguist who studied at Yale College (circa 1840–1842) and under Edward Elbridge Salisbury in 1849. He held posts at Middlebury College (1844–1845) and Yale University (1845–1872).

James Haughton Woods (1864–1935) was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at Harvard College, Strasbourg, and under Charles Rockwell Lanman, Arthur Venis, and Mukunda Shastri Adkar, later serving as Professor at Harvard University (circa 1903–1914).

James Irving Manatt (1845–1915) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Grinnell and Yale under William Dwight Whitney, and held posts at Denison, Marietta, University of Nebraska–Lincoln, the United States, and Brown University (circa 1892–1915).

James Ishmael Ford is a Buddhist and religious studies figure who founded Boundless Way Zen. He studied under Houn Jiyu-Kennett (circa 1970–1977) and John Tarrant (circa 1987–1998), and attended the Pacific School of Religion (circa 1988–1991).

James J. Y. Liu (1926–1986) was a sinologist who studied at Fu Jen, Tsinghua, Bristol, and Oxford. He taught at London, New Asia College, Hong Kong, Hawaii, Pittsburgh, Chicago, and Stanford University (circa 1967–1986).

James Kenneth Powell II is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Northwestern (BA), the University of Chicago (M.Div.), and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD, circa 1988–1998). His teachers included David Tracy, David M. Knipe, Isshi Yamada, and Geshe Lhundub Sopa.

James L. Fitzgerald is an Indologist who served as Professor at the University of Tennessee from circa 1983 to 2005. In circa 2006, he became Das Professor of Sanskrit in the Department of Classics at Brown University.

James Mallinson is an Indology and religious studies scholar. Educated at Eton and the University of Oxford (D.Phil. 1995–2003) under Alexis Sanderson, he served as Lecturer in Sanskrit and Classical Indian Studies at SOAS University of London (2013–2016).

James Mark Shields is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He became Associate Professor of Comparative Humanities and Asian Thought at Bucknell University in circa 2006 and served as an Overseas Collaborative Researcher at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.

James Matthew Baskind specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at Yale University from circa 2000 to 2006 under doctoral supervisor Stanley Weinstein.

James McHugh is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Cambridge, Oxford, and Harvard (PhD circa 2003–2008). Mentored by Stephanie W. Jamison and others, he held posts at Cornell University and the University of Southern California (circa 2008).
